                                      PRICES ORDER No. 154

                                                being
APRICES ORDER relating to the maximum wholesale and retail price for

                                               BREAD

                                    LAE AND PORT MORESBY

   Made by the price Controller under the provisions of the Prices
Regulation Act 1949, as amended to date, to
   come into operation on the date of publication in the National
Gazette.

 1. CITATION.
   This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 154.

2. REVOCATION.

   Prices Order No. 134 and Prices Order No. 135 are hereby revoked.

3. DEFINITIONS.
   In this Order—

     "bread" means a product obtained by baking a yeast leavened
dough prepared with flour and water with or
          without other ingredients;

     "ordinary bread" means bread made into loaves other than
starch-reduced bread, protein-increased bread or
          milk bread as defined in this Order or fancy bread;

     "milk bread" means bread which is made into loaves and which
contains no less than four parts per centum
          by weight of non-fat milk solids calculated on the water-
free substance;
     "starch-reduced bread" or "protein increased bread" means bread
which is made into loaves and which
          contains not less than two and seven-tenths parts per
centum by weight of nitrogen calculated on the
          water-free substance;

     "unwrapped" in relation to the sale of any bread means that
such bread is not wrapped as defined in this
          Order;

     "wrapped" means in relation    to the sale of any bread that such
bread is fully enclosed prior to    delivery to
           the place at which the   bread is sold by retail, in waxed
or grease-proof paper, cellulose    film, polythene or
           other similar wrapping   and that such bread was so enclosed
when sold;


 National Gazette                                                5
No. 21-20th November, 1975


                                              Prices Order No. 154--
continued

        "foil-wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread
that such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery

             to the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in
aluminium or other foil, and that such bread was

             so enclosed when sold.

4. MEASUREMENT OF WEIGHT.

     Where, in this Order, the maximum price fixed is related to the
weight of bread, the weight is to be measured

 when the bread is cold.

     5. MAXIMUM PRICE.

     The maximum price at which bread included in a category
described in the first column of the Schedule to this

 Order may be sold by wholesale and retail in the cities of Lae and
Port Moresby is the price specified in the second

column of that Schedule opposite to the description of that
category.

     6. DISPLAY OF PRICES.

     A person or organisation engaged in selling bread by retail in
the Cities of Lae and Port Moresby, shall dis-

play in each of their places of business, in prominent positions and
in large clear and legible figures, the types of

bread loaves covered by this Order and the prices at which such
loaves may be bought.

    Improvements:—Section 57 of the Land Act 1962-74 provides that
an Agricultural Lease shall contain conditions prescribing

the minimum improvements to- be carried out by the lessee.
Conditions applicable to the lease described above are as follows:


       (a) Of the land suitable for cultivation, the following
proportions shall be planted in a good and husbandlike manner with

           a crop or crops of economic value, which shall be
harvested regularly in accordance with sound commercial practice:


            One-half in the first period of 5 years of the term;


            Four-fifths in the first period of 10 years of the term;


           and during the remainder of the term four-fifths of the
land so suitable shall be kept so planted.


       (b) Provided always that if at the end of the first two years
of the term, the lessee has not made such progress with the

           land preparation and plantings as to suggest that he will
fulfil the improvement conditions, the Minister for Lands after

           considering any reply from the lessee to a demand to show

                                                   PRICES ORDER No. 155

                                                                    being
A PRICES ORDER relating to the maximum retail price for

                               PETROL, DISTILLATE AND LIGHTING
KEROSENE

     Made by the Deputy Price Controller under the provisions of the
Prices Regulation Aet-1949, as amended to
     date, to come into operation on the date of publication in the
National Gazette.
1. CITATION.

This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 155.
2. REVOCATION.
     The Prices Orders specified in Schedule 2 of this Order are
revoked.
3. DEFINITIONS.
     In this Order—
         "petrol" includes any substance normally sold as petrol
whether or not containing additives of any kind;
         "distillate" includes any substance normally sold as
automotive distillate whether or not containing additives
              of any kind;
         "kerosene" includes any substance normally sold as kerosene
being a medium refined petroleum product as
              used for lighting and cooking in home appliances,
whether or not containing additives of any kind;
         "wholesaler" in relation to petrol, distillate or lighting
kerosene means a person or a firm who sells petrol,
              distillate or lighting kerosene for the purpose of
resale and not for the purpose of use;
         "supplier" in relation to petrol, distillate or lighting
kerosene, means a person or a firm who sells petrol,
              distillate or lighting kerosene for the purpose of use;
         "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.

4. MAXIMUM PRICE.

      (i) Subject to Subclause (ii) of this clause, where petrol,
distillate or kerosene is supplied-

        (a) at a locality specified in the first column of Schedule
I to this Order; or

        (b) at some other place at which the petrol, distillate or
lighting kerosene is transported from any such
             locality by or on behalf of a wholesaler, or supplier;

the maximum price per gallon at which the petrol, distillate or
kerosene may be supplied is the sum of-

        (c) the maximum retail selling price specified in the
Second, Third or Fourth Column as the case may be, of
             Schedule I in relation to the locality concerned; and

        (d) the amount (if any) charged for the transport referred
to in paragraph (b) of this subclause.

(ii) Where the maximum price of any quantity of petrol,
distillate or kerosene supplied at any one time, cal-
culated in accordance with Subclause (i) of this clause is an amount
involving a fraction of a toea, the supplier
may charge to the next whole toea.

5. SUPPLY TO GOVERNMENT ETC.

     Nothing in this Order applies to or relates to the supply of
petrol, distillate or kerosene to the Government or
instrumentality or authority of the Government.

6. DISPLAY OF PRICES.

     A person or an organisation engaged in selling petrol,
distillate or lighting kerosene by retail shall display in
each of the places of business in prominent positions and in large
clear and legible figures the maximum prices
at which such petrol, distillate and kerosene may be bought.

Improvements:—Section 57 of the Land Act 1962-1974 (as amended)
provides that an Agricultural Lease shall contain con-

 ditions prescribing the minimum improvement to be carried out by
the lessee. Conditions applicable to the lease described above are

 as follows:


        (a) Of the land suitable for cultivation, the following
proportions shall be planted in a good and husbandlike manner

            with a crop or crops of economic value, which shall be
harvested regularly in accordance with sound commercial.

               practice:

                 One-half in the first period of 5 years of the term;

                 Four-fifths in the first period of 10 years of the
term;

            and during the remainder of the term four-fifths of the
land so suitable shall be kept so planted.

        (b) Provided always that if at the end of the first 2 years
of the term the lessee has not made such progress

            with the land preparation and plantings as to suggest
that he will fulfil the improvement conditions, the Minister

            for Lands after considering any reply from the lessee to
a demand to show cause why he (the Minister) should

            not so do may, by notice in the National Gazette and in
accordance with the Land Act as amended to date, forfeit

               the lease.

        (c) The lessee or his agent shall take up residency or
occupancy of the block within six months of date of grant.

        (d) The Minister for Lands may, after considering the
recommendation of the Land Board and the detailed proposals of

            an applicant given in evidence to the Board, vary the
above condition.

        (e) The Minister, for Lands may, after considering the
recommendation of the Land Board approve payments for the

            improvements in not more than ten equal annual
instalments with interest at 5 per cent per annum payable on the

amount outstanding.

formulation or research in
